To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NO and cGMP activate type II cGMK in cells of neuronal origin to regulate gene expression.
NO and cGMP activate the fos promoter in neuronal and glia cells through G‐kinase‐II‐mediated phosphorylation of the CREB transcription factor.
NO‐ and cAMP‐induced activation and inactivation of the fos promoter is mediated by G‐kinases II and I, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of gene regulation by nitric oxide and cAMP‐ and cG‐dependent protein kinases (PKs).
the regulation of gene expression by NO/cGMP and the role that this pathway may play in mediating the effects of NO on synaptic plasticity and neuronal function.

elucidation of mechanisms of signal transduction and transcriptional regulation in the central nervous system, and we are particularly interested in understanding how nitric oxide (NO), a gaseous neurotransmitter and neuromodulator, regulates gene expression in neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have provided evidence that cGMP‐activated G‐kinase type II is involved in gene regulation in neurons and glial cells.
the NO/cGMP‐dependent pathway is a major mechanism of signal transduction in the nervous system that controls gene expression by regulating the activity of the type II cGmp‐kinase.
the NO/cGMP pathway regulates transcription in neuronal and glia cells by a G‐kinase‐dependent mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cGMP regulates neuronal and glial gene expression by activating type II G‐kinase, which is membrane associated and does not translocate to nucleus, whereas type I G‐kinase is soluble and can regulate gene expression in fibrous cells.
cGMP‐activated protein kinases (G‐kinases) regulate gene expression in cells of neuronal or glial origin.
cGMP‐activated type II cGmp kinase regulates the expression of genes that are involved in cell proliferation, differentiation and survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of nitric oxide and cAMP on gene expression in the nervous system may be mediated by different cGMP‐kinases, and that these effects may not be mediated by calcium uptake.
cGMP and G‐kinase regulate gene expression in the brain by different mechanisms, depending on the cell type.
cGMP‐mediated gene regulation is not restricted to neuronal cells, but is also found in glial cells.
